verdict: This is a different class of document from round 1. The contrast table in §7.2 is the proof: I recomputed all 27 pairs with the WCAG 2.1 formula and every single number is exact, including the dark-mode primary at 13.73:1 that shipped at 1.96:1 last round. The phone portrait budget in §5.1a adds up to 734/702/553/763 band for band, the walk budget in §5.1c adds up, iPad portrait and landscape in §5.2/§5.3 add up, the 33 title attributes each have a named text home, the four icon-only controls are each replaced by a word, and the achromatic turn in §7.1 is argued rather than asserted — the one surviving hue is confined to three places and told why. As a painter: the swatch is finally sized (48 x 56, on paper, at wash strength, with that sentence in writing twice), the water ratio has moved into the row's primary line, `Then: let it dry completely.` is budgeted into the first 164 px, the step position survives the afternoon, there is a `Painted` tick, and `New photo` is 24 px and a confirm dialog away from `Save`. That is the difference between planning at the table and trusting it at the easel, and it mostly crosses over. What stops me signing it: the document proves heights obsessively and never once proves a width, and the one row that matters most — the selected plan row — cannot hold what §9.6 puts in it at 390 px. `Full size`, the state in which the painter actually looks at the picture, is specified to overflow the viewport by about 90 px. A `max-height: 44rem` rule written for an iPhone SE fires on a 1024 x 768 iPad in landscape and shrinks the colour-comparison fields to 60 px on the device the brief calls primary, which undoes painter must-fix 4 on the exact screen it was raised about. And acceptance criterion 10 forbids rem literals in component files while §9 is written in them. These are local faults in a structurally sound design — nothing here needs re-architecting, it needs a width pass, a media-query guard and an honest re-read of §20 against §9. Round 3 should be short.
mustFix: §5.1e, phone full size, overflows the viewport by roughly 90 px, and it is the state the painter uses most at the easel. `--picture-max: calc(100svh - 11.2rem - env(...))` accounts for the 48 px app bar and the 56 px tab bar and one 8 px gap only. But the section also says `the stage bar's button reads Fit`, so `stage__bar` (48) is still rendered, plus at least two more 8 px gaps. On a 734 px viewport: 48 + 8 + 48 + 8 + 622 + 56 = 790. The bottom of the picture sits under the tab bar, which contradicts acceptance criterion 1 (`the picture is visible without scrolling`) and criterion 3 (`no layout overflows its viewport`). It is also unstated whether `picture__readout` renders in this state; if it does, add 48 more. Subtract the stage bar and every gap explicitly, say what happens to the readout, and give the sum for 734, 702 and 553 like every other state gets.

§9.6 `plan__sub` cannot be built at phone width, and it is the band that carries wash selection — the thing the painter taps to pick a strength. It is `display: flex; gap: var(--gap-05x); min-height: var(--touch)` with no wrap rule, no overflow rule and no min-widths, holding three children: `plan__bar` with a `plate` per paint (two plates reading `1 x 663`, `2 x 485` need about 124 px), up to five `plan__wash` buttons which §6 and criterion 5 require to be 48 x 48 (240 px plus 32 px of gaps), and the `Painted` switch (24 px box plus the word, about 90 px). That is roughly 500 px of content in the 342 px the row has on a 390 px iPhone, 286 px in layer mode once the 48 px tick column is taken. Either the washes shrink below 48 px, breaking §6 and criterion 5, or the band wraps and the selected row stops being 56 + 8 + 48. §9.2 gave `stage__bar` an explicit non-wrapping scroll rule for exactly this reason; `plan__sub` needs the same treatment, with the width arithmetic written out at 375 and 390 px for five washes, and `Painted` moved out of the band if it does not fit.

The `max-height: 44rem` short-screen variant is unguarded by width, so a rule written for an iPhone SE fires on the primary device. 44rem in a media query is 704 px (§4.1 states this trap itself), and §5's own working-height table gives a 1024 x 768 iPad in landscape 698 px and a 1280 x 800 laptop window well under 704. Three things then change where they must not: `detail__field` drops from 80 px to 60 px and `detail__head` from 48 to 40 (§9.7), which reintroduces painter must-fix 4 — too small a patch to judge a mix against — on the iPad and on most laptops; and `--panel-min` drops to 176 (§5.1a). Guard all three with `(max-width: 47.999rem)`, and restate §5.1b's short-screen row as phone-only.

§5.1a's 702 px column contradicts its own CSS. The 375 x 812 phone in Safari is given 702 px of working height, which is below the 704 px `max-height: 44rem` threshold, so `--panel-min` is 176, not 240. The formula then yields a picture of min(36svh = 252, 702 - 224 - 176 = 302) = 252 and a panel region of 226 px — not the 238/240 the table prints, and below the 240 px that acceptance criterion 1 demands. Either the threshold moves (40rem = 640 px would clear both 702 and 734 and still catch the 553 px SE) or the table is wrong; as written the spec fails its own criterion 1 on an iPhone 13 mini.

§5.1d double-counts the bottom safe-area inset, so phone landscape gives away 21 px of picture it has. The working-height table defines the standalone landscape case as 390 - 0 - 21 = 369, i.e. the inset is already excluded; the budget then lists `app__tabs (+ bottom inset)` as 48 + 21 inside a column that sums to 369. The CSS `calc(100svh - 4.8rem - 4.8rem - var(--gap-05x) * 3 - env(safe-area-inset-bottom))` with 100svh = 390 gives 249 px of picture, not the 228 printed, and the panel column 257, not 236. Pick one basis — full-screen svh with insets subtracted, or a pre-reduced working height — and apply it in §5.1a, §5.1d and §5.2 alike; §5.2's standalone column has the opposite inconsistency, computing 42svh against 1004 where §5.1a computes 36svh against 844.

§5.1b's recipe budget, the number §3.3 cites as the proof the whole round turns on, is built from an element that does not exist. `detail__head 48 + gap 8 + caption 20 + two 80 px colour fields + gap 8 + recipe line 44 = 208` — but §9.7's element list for `detail` contains no `recipe line`; the first thing under the compare pair is `detail__subtitle` (`--fs-medium`, 600) followed by `detail__recipe` at `min-height: 5.6rem`. The real figure is 48 + 8 + 20 + 80 + 8 + 18 + 56 = 238, which still clears 246 on a 390 px iPhone but fails the 240 px floor at 702 and the 176 px short variant (40 + 8 + 60 + 8 + 18 + 56 = 190 against 176). Name the element in §9.7 with its height, or rebuild the sum from the elements that are specified.

No budget anywhere accounts for the selected row, and selection is the normal state in the loop §3.3 claims to prove. §5.1b's `Colours` row reads `plan__head 48 + three rows of 56 with 8 px between them = 240`, and §3.3 step 4 promises `the head and three full rows are visible` — but step 2 of that same loop selected area 12, so one of those rows carries the 48 px `plan__sub` band plus its 8 px row-gap and is 112 px tall, not 56. The real content is 48 + 8 + 112 + 8 + 56 + 8 + 56 = 296 against 246 px of panel. Either say that the head, the selected row and one neighbour are visible, or make the sub band part of the row height. The same omission runs through §5.2 and §5.3.

§14.1's accessible-name pattern silently deletes the state words that §7.2 and §9.6 rely on to satisfy `state is never carried by colour alone`. The name given for `plan__row` is `Colour 7, 1 part 663 Sepia brown plus 2 parts 485 Indigo, 23 percent of the image, 4 washes` — it stops before `selected`, `painting now`, `painted` and `Not needed for this picture`, all of which §9.6 puts in `plan__meta` inside the row button. If that name is set with `aria-label` it overrides the element's content, so a screen-reader user is told nothing about muted or painted rows at all (`aria-pressed` covers only selected, `aria-current="step"` only the walk's current layer), and `painted` is exposed nowhere else because the `Painted` checkbox exists only on the selected row. Append the state clause to the name pattern, or specify the name as computed from content rather than overridden.

Acceptance criterion 10 contradicts §9. `grep -rn "rem" src/css/components/ returns nothing; every size comes from a token` is unsatisfiable against the component CSS this document actually writes: `3.2rem` and `4.8rem` grid columns and `5.6rem` row height (§9.6), `6rem` and `10rem` option min-widths (§9.4, §9.10), `6.4rem` and `14rem` chips (§9.10), `7.2rem` thumbnails (§9.13), `18rem` collection cells (§9.15), `96rem` dialog width (§9.11), `2.4rem` checkbox, `3rem` thumb, `1rem` track, `0.6rem` plate padding, `0.3rem`/`0.2rem` focus ring. §4.3's rule names only `--fs-*`, `--gap*`, `--max-width`, `--article-width`, `--rail`, `--touch`, `--touch-primary` as sources, which covers maybe half of these. Define the missing tokens (a chip width, a thumbnail height, a number-column width, a ring width) or rewrite criterion 10 to forbid rem literals for type and spacing only. Round 1 was marked down for criteria its own body contradicted.

The card — the container every budget in §5 is measured inside — is never specified. `plan card`, `detail card`, `source card`, `settings card` are referenced throughout; §7.6 gives `--m-vert: 24` between cards and §8 gives `card titles` a type role; §4.3 maps `panel__title` to `--fs-large` and §18 deletes `_panel.css` — but no block in §9 defines a card's padding, background, border, radius or head height, §17's components.css list has no `card.css` or `panel.css`, and `ui.css` is annotated `button, card, link, plate, focus ring` with no values. Every §5 budget implicitly assumes zero vertical padding: add the conventional 16 px top and bottom and the Recipe tab becomes 240 against a 240 px floor. Specify the block, then re-run the sums.
shouldFix: §9.3: the one line a painter reads from across the table is the faintest and smallest thing in the design, and it truncates mid-recipe on the device this round was written for. `picture__readout` is `--fs-small` (14 px) in `--c-copy-light`, `white-space: nowrap; text-overflow: ellipsis`. The specified string `12 · 23% of image · 1 x 663 Sepia brown + 2 x 485 Indigo` is about 56 characters, roughly 400 px at 14 px, in 374 px of content on a 390 px iPhone — so it renders as `12 · 23% of image · 1 x 663 Sepia…` and the second paint, the one I am about to pick up, is the part that is cut. The 40 px band holds two 14 px lines at 1.4 with 11 px to spare. Allow two lines, drop the percentage below 400 px, and set it in `--c-copy`: §9.6 promoted the water ratio out of the faint type for exactly this reason and then left the readout behind.

§9.9: `Hide hints` and `Hide` sit in the same 48 px `settings__group-head`, 8 px apart, and differ by one word while doing entirely different things — one dismisses a paragraph for good on this device, the other folds the group. That is the confusable pair the rest of the document is careful to avoid. Rename the fold to `Fold` / `Unfold`, or move `Hide hints` to the end of the hint paragraph it dismisses, where it is beside its own object.

§9.12: `paintbox__readout` is the only surface in the entire app for `nameDe` and the free-text stock note (`last pan, nearly out`), and it is fed by `the last-tapped chip` — but tapping a chip toggles the paint in or out of the box. To read whether a pan is nearly out I must first change my selection and then change it back. Feed the readout from a non-destructive source, or give the chip a second affordance. Related: `paintbox__group` for `Selected paints` is `pinned above the filter, always visible` with no height cap, while `paintbox__count` can read `54 paints selected` — 54 pinned chips at 64 px is the whole dialog. Cap it and make it scroll, or show a count and a `Show` button.

§9.6 and §15.3: `plan__painted` exists only on the selected row, so recording that I have finished layer 3 costs me a selection — which in layer mode solos that layer and changes what the picture shows, and in mix mode shows only that mix's washes. Three taps and a changed view for a bookkeeping action, performed with a wet brush in the other hand. Put `Painted` in the detail card head or in `walk__nav` next to `Next`, where the painter already is when a wash is done.

§3.4 and §5.1c: on the phone the walk takes over the `Spot` tab, so while the walk is open there is no detail card and §2.1's `Detail` place does not exist. The spec never says what tapping the picture does then — the readout gives `Spot · 3 layers · match: good` and there is nowhere to see which layers cover that spot. That is a real question mid-walk (`have I already glazed this bit?`). State it: either the tap is inert during the walk and say so in the readout, or the walk's panel gains a spot block.

§6.3 and §9.6: focus and selection are nearly the same mark. The focus ring is `0.3rem solid var(--c-focus)` at `outline-offset: 0.2rem`, and `--c-focus` is `#221f1c`, which is `--c-copy`; the selected row is `0.2rem solid var(--c-copy)` at `outline-offset: -0.2rem`. On a keyboard a focused unselected row and an unfocused selected row differ by 1 px of width, 4 px of offset and a 2 px white backing band. Make one of them dashed, or give the ring a visibly different geometry.

§9.1 and §14.1 give the phone tab bar the wrong semantics and leave the panels undefined. Four `button`s with `aria-current="page"` is the pattern for navigation between pages; these switch panels within one page. Nothing says the panels have ids, `role="tabpanel"`, `aria-controls`, or whether the inactive ones are removed from the accessibility tree — and §18 only adds `activeTab` local state. Specify a tablist with `aria-selected` and `aria-controls`, or `aria-pressed` with labelled regions. Acceptance criterion 15 asserts the screen-reader experience is covered; this is the hole in it.

§14.3 puts `app__tabs` last in the phone focus order, after the active tab panel. With 20 plan rows, each a button, plus a selected row's bar and checkbox, reaching `Settings` by keyboard or switch control is roughly 25 stops. DOM order matching visual order is the right instinct; a tab bar is the exception. Either put the tablist first in the DOM and position it visually, or give it a skip link.

§9's own preamble is not kept: `Every block lists its states: default, hover, active, focus-visible, disabled, selected, busy — where a state does not apply it is marked n/a`. Three blocks do it (`app__tabs`, `plan__row`, `detail`, partly `button`/`segmented`). `stage`, `picture`, `viewbar`, `showsheet`, `source`, `settings`, `control`, `closeup`, `paintbox`, `collection`, `confirm`, `consent`, `gate`, `chip`, `switch` and `swatch` have none, and the brief names the state inventory as a deliverable. Either finish the lists or delete the promise.

`--c-plate` is `#ffffff` in both themes, and §9.3 makes `picture__pane` a plate too. In dark mode that means a brilliant white sheet behind the photo, a white plate behind every swatch, under every wash letter, under every bar label, on every one of 54 paint chips and inside both detail fields — 16.60:1 against the card, which the table reports as a pass. It is defensible (paint on paper is white paper) and it is the honest way to show a wash, but nobody has written down what the evening studio case looks like with that much white in it. Say it is deliberate and state the one mitigation you are willing to make — a dimmed plate for non-swatch labels, or none.

§9.4: inside one sheet, tapping a view option applies it and closes the sheet while `Outlines`, `Numbers` and `Full size` leave it open. Two dismissal rules in one surface is a small thing to learn and an easy thing to get wrong with gloves on. Also, on a 553 px phone the sheet is capped at 70svh = 387 px and its body is roughly 480 px, so `Outlines` and `Numbers` — which §2.3 calls first level, one labelled tap away — are one tap plus a scroll. Worth one sentence of the same honesty §2.3 applies to Setup.

§5.3 proves the sticky block fits on an iPad in landscape and never proves the loop. At 698 px the free space below the sticky block at rest is 67 px, and scrolled fully the rail shows about 179 px — against a detail card that §5.1b measures at 208 (238 by its own elements). The brief calls the iPad the primary device and ux must-fix 2 was about this screen. Give §5.3 a §5.1b-style content table: what of the rail is readable with the picture, in landscape, in both modes.

Acceptance criterion 9 enumerates the directional rules in the design and misses one it declares elsewhere: §7.2 lists `the rule between the two colour fields in the detail card` among `--c-border`'s uses, and §9.7 specifies it. Implemented the obvious way that is a `border-inline-start` and the grep returns two hits, not `exactly one`. Add it to the enumeration or specify the divider as a gap with a background.
genericRisk: Much reduced, and reduced by decisions rather than by adjectives. Killing the trust blue is the single most convincing thing in the round: §7.1 replaces it with graphite, §7.3 confines the one surviving hue to three places that are never beside a swatch, and §7.4 declares `--c-accent` and `--c-success` as aliases with the reason instead of quietly inventing a green. Radii at 2-4 px, a square-cornered white picture pane with a hairline, the column rule after `plan__number` so the list reads as a paint chart rather than a stack of cards, and the deletion of all four icon-only controls are real departures from the default shape. The `plate` in §7.2 is the one genuinely invented object in the document — a written label on paper laid over paint is what a paint chart does, and it falls out of a contrast constraint rather than a mood. What still gives it away: the silhouette is unchanged in kind — fixed app bar, white cards on a tint, four-item bottom tab bar, segmented controls on every row, a bottom sheet, a `More` group at the end of Setup, which is the standard mobile-app furniture drawer the painter objected to `AI help` living in. §2.1's five named places are five cards with heads; nothing about the layout above the component level says watercolour. The copy is doing most of the work that the structure is not — `1:4 with water, like tea`, `Leave the paper white.`, `Swatches are one stroke on white paper` are the lines a painter wrote, and they sit inside an app shell any tool could wear. The second tell is quieter and worth naming because round 1 was caught by its cousin: this document proves heights to the pixel in six places and never proves a single width, and the three widths I checked by hand (the selected row's sub band, the readout string, the chip grid's `about 1 700 px` which is 1 944) are all wrong. Numbers that look checked because their neighbours were is the same signature, just moved one axis over.
buildable: Close, and much closer than round 1. A competent implementer can build most of this without inventing: §4.3 maps all 39 rem values file and line, §11 homes all 33 title attributes with the dynamic ones traced to the line that builds them, §12 leaves no string to write, §14.1 gives real markup, §18 is a per-file migration table, §17 is the import order. What they would still have to invent, in order of how much it costs: (1) the card block — padding, border, background, head height, the thing every §5 budget is measured inside, specified nowhere; (2) the behaviour of `plan__sub` when its contents exceed the row width, which they always do on a phone — wrap, scroll or shrink are three different designs and the spec picks none; (3) whether `stage__bar` and `picture__readout` render in `app--picture-full`, and what the corrected `--picture-max` is; (4) about nine missing size tokens that acceptance criterion 10 demands exist (chip width, thumbnail height, number-column width, track height, thumb size, ring widths, plate padding, dialog width, collection cell); (5) where `app__notice` goes in phone landscape, where §5.1d hides the app bar it is specified to hang under; (6) the tab/panel ARIA relationship; (7) how the confirm dialog is raised — §13 says `raised by pro-style imperative code from the component that owns the action` and §18 gives `ConfirmDialog.vue` props and events but no owner, no mounting point and no promise-style contract, so seven call sites will each invent one; (8) `layout.move('painted', {'7': true})` assumes `move()` accepts an arbitrary object in a map named `positions` — stated, not shown, and if the store validates a position shape the whole persistence section fails. None of these is structural. All of them are an afternoon of writing, and the right sequence is: fix the five arithmetic errors, do a width pass at 375 px on every row the document specifies, then re-read §20 line by line against §9 and delete or satisfy each criterion the body contradicts.
regressions: Painter must-fix 4 (the swatch) is answered in the plan row and then half-undone in the detail card on the primary device: `detail__field` drops to 60 px under `max-height: 44rem`, a query with no width guard that fires on a 1024 x 768 iPad in landscape (698 px per §5's own table) and on most laptop windows. The patch I judge a mix against is the small variant everywhere except a phone held in portrait.

UX must-fix 4 (the 40 px wash segment) is answered in §6's touch table — 48 px hit area, 40 px painted band — and then made unbuildable by §9.6, which puts five of those 48 px buttons plus a ratio bar plus a `Painted` switch into a single non-wrapping 342 px flex band. The criterion is satisfied in the table and contradicted in the component, which is the same shape of defect round 1 was marked down for.

UX must-fix 1 and painter must-fix 1 (the phone budget) are genuinely rebuilt, but the one state that was not budgeted is the one the budget exists to protect: `Full size` in §5.1e overflows by about 90 px, and the selected plan row — the state the §3.3 loop is in from step 2 onwards — is 56 px taller than every table counts. The arithmetic improved enormously; it is still not complete.

UX must-fix 2 (iPad arithmetic) is answered for the sticky block and not for the loop. §5.2 and §5.3 prove the stage can never exceed the viewport, which was the stated failure, but the brief's primary device gets no §5.1b-style proof that the picture and the recipe are on screen together; §5.3's own figure is 67 px of rail visible at rest, and about 179 px scrolled, against a detail card of 208 to 238.

UX shouldFix 2 asked for the text-on-paint rule and also for the honest deletion of unmeasured claims. §7.2 delivers both and is exact — but the focus ring is then claimed to `read on a photo, on paint and on paper` while the table measures it only against `--c-focus-backing` and `--c-surface`. The two-tone construction makes the claim plausible; it is still an assertion in a section whose whole point is that assertions were replaced by measurements.
